description: A doctoral research seminar on sequential decision making when outcomes and observations are uncertain, from Markov decision processes and POMDPs to online planning, learned models and safety. Students read and critique recent papers, implement solvers, probe their limits experimentally, and write a research proposal.
modelledOn: Puterman, Markov Decision Processes: Discrete Stochastic Dynamic Programming
Kochenderfer, Wheeler and Wray, Algorithms for Decision Making
Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
Bertsekas, Dynamic Programming and Optimal Control
outcomes: Prove convergence properties of dynamic programming methods for MDPs and state their dependence on the discount factor.
Explain the computational hardness of partially observable and decentralised problems and compare exact, point-based and online solvers.
Implement and analyse sampling-based planners such as sparse sampling, UCT and belief-tree search.
Critique methods for hierarchical planning, learned models and model-based reinforcement learning, including their failure modes.
Formulate safety and risk requirements with constrained, robust and risk-sensitive objectives and verify them.
Write a research proposal that identifies an open problem, a benchmark and an evaluation plan.

units.title: Markov decision processes
topics: MDP definition, policies, value functions and Bellman equations
Value iteration and policy iteration; the contraction mapping argument
Linear programming formulation and its dual
Discounted, average-reward and stochastic shortest path criteria
Approximate dynamic programming and error bounds with function approximation
Seminar: reading classic and recent convergence results

units.title: Partially observable models
topics: POMDPs, belief states and the piecewise-linear convex value function
Exact solution with alpha vectors and the complexity of POMDPs
Point-based solvers: PBVI, HSVI and SARSOP
Decentralised POMDPs and multi-agent decision problems
Belief representations: particles, predictive states and recurrent policies

units.title: Online and Monte Carlo planning
topics: Sparse sampling and bounds independent of state-space size
UCT and regret analysis of Monte Carlo tree search
POMCP, DESPOT and belief-tree search
Continuous spaces: progressive widening and continuous-action search
Anytime and receding-horizon planning under real-time limits

units.title: Hierarchical and temporal planning
topics: Options and semi-Markov decision processes
MAXQ and task hierarchies
Temporal logic specifications and product MDPs
Temporal planning with durative actions and concurrency
Skill discovery and abstraction

units.title: Planning with learned models
topics: Model-based reinforcement learning: Dyna and ensemble models
Latent-space planning and value-equivalent models
Compounding model error and the simulation lemma
Bayesian reinforcement learning, exploration and posterior sampling
Offline reinforcement learning and pessimism
Open problems: model misspecification and distribution shift

units.title: Safe and risk-sensitive decisions
topics: Constrained MDPs and Lagrangian methods
Risk measures: CVaR, entropic risk and mean-variance
Robust MDPs and uncertainty sets
Shielding, safe exploration and barrier functions
Probabilistic model checking of policies

units.title: Planning for robots and agents
topics: Motion planning under uncertainty: belief-space planning and chance constraints
Task and motion planning
Language-model agents as planners and the role of verification
Multi-agent coordination and humans in the loop
Case studies: crop-spraying drones, ambulance dispatch and clinic supply planning

units.title: Research proposal
topics: Finding a gap in the literature
Formulating hypotheses and designing a benchmark
Writing the proposal and the evaluation plan
Panel questions and peer review

schedule.title: MDPs and Bellman equations
schedule.exercise: Prove that the Bellman optimality operator is a contraction in the max norm, and compute two sweeps of value iteration by hand on a small MDP.

tasks.title: Step value iteration on a 3x3 stochastic grid world, recording the value table after iterations 1, 2 and 10 and the greedy policy
Compute the error after each value iteration sweep on a 20-state MDP and compare it with the gamma-to-the-k contraction bound
Compare policy iteration, value iteration and modified policy iteration on random MDPs with 100 to 1000 states and plot sweeps and time to convergence

schedule.title: Linear programming and other criteria
schedule.exercise: Write the primal and dual linear programs of a small MDP, interpret the dual variables as state-action visitation frequencies, and explain when average reward and discounted criteria give different policies.

tasks.title: Solve the linear program of a 4-state MDP, compare its solution with value iteration and read the dual variables as occupancy measures
Find the optimal policy of a machine replacement MDP under discount factors 0.9, 0.99 and 0.999, and show where the policy changes
Solve a stochastic shortest path problem with dead ends using value iteration, show where it fails without a proper-policy assumption, and fix it

schedule.title: Approximation and the research literature
schedule.exercise: Present a recent paper on approximate dynamic programming, state its main bound in your own words, find an assumption that is hard to check in practice, and run a small experiment that probes it.

tasks.title: Fit a linear value function to a 50-state chain MDP by fitted value iteration and plot the error against the number of features
Show fitted value iteration diverging for a chosen feature set on a small MDP, then repair it and report the Bellman error before and after
Reproduce a figure from a recent approximate dynamic programming paper at small scale, and report which of its claims your results support

schedule.title: POMDPs and exact solutions
schedule.exercise: Update beliefs in a two-state tiger-style POMDP for a sequence of observations, draw its alpha vectors for horizon three, and explain why exact solving is PSPACE-hard.

tasks.title: Update the belief in a two-state sensor POMDP for five actions and observations, and plot the belief against time
Compute the horizon-3 alpha vectors of a small POMDP step by step and plot the piecewise-linear value function over the belief
Implement point-based value iteration with 50 belief points on a 10-state POMDP and compare value with the exact solution at horizon 5

schedule.title: Decentralised problems and belief representations
schedule.exercise: Show with a two-agent example why decentralised problems are harder than single-agent POMDPs, and compare particle beliefs with a recurrent policy on a partially observed navigation task.

tasks.title: Evaluate two joint policies of a two-agent clinic delivery problem with no communication, and compute the expected team reward of each
Track belief with 100 and 1000 particles on a noisy localisation task and compare the error and the degeneracy of the particle set
Train a recurrent policy on a partially observed grid task and compare it with a belief-based policy on return and sample efficiency

schedule.title: Sparse sampling and UCT
schedule.exercise: Derive the depth and width needed by sparse sampling for a target accuracy, state the regret behaviour of UCT, and explain how POMCP handles belief without enumerating states.

tasks.title: Run sparse sampling with different widths on a small MDP and plot the value estimate error against the number of samples
Implement UCT for a 10x10 grid MDP, vary the exploration constant and report the value reached against simulation budget
Implement POMCP on a rock sampling problem, compare it with a point-based solver and report return against planning time

schedule.title: Continuous spaces and real-time planning
schedule.exercise: Use progressive widening to plan in a continuous action space, and design an anytime planner with a fixed time budget for a control loop at 10 Hz.

tasks.title: Run a receding-horizon planner on a car-following task with horizons 1, 3 and 8 and record the cost and computation per step
Add progressive widening to tree search for a one-dimensional continuous action problem and compare with a fixed discretisation
Build an anytime planner that stops at a 100 ms deadline and measure how decision quality improves with the time budget

schedule.title: Options, hierarchies and temporal specifications
schedule.exercise: Define options for a two-room task and show how they change planning depth, build a product MDP for a temporal logic goal, and compare temporal planners on a durative-action domain.

tasks.title: Add door-seeking options to a two-room grid world and compare value iteration iterations with and without the options
Build a product MDP of a grid world and a temporal logic goal, solve for the policy maximising satisfaction probability and report it
Learn bottleneck states as option subgoals from trajectories in a four-room task and test whether they speed up learning over primitive actions

schedule.title: Model-based RL and compounding error
schedule.exercise: State the simulation lemma and show its bound on a learned model, then compare a Dyna agent with a model-free agent on sample efficiency and an ensemble model with a single model.

tasks.title: Run Dyna with 0, 5 and 50 planning steps per real step on a grid task and plot the return against real interactions
Roll a learned model forward for 1 to 50 steps, measure prediction error growth against the true system and compare with the theoretical bound
Train a latent dynamics model that predicts only reward and value, plan in it with tree search and compare with a pixel-level model

schedule.title: Exploration, offline learning and open problems
schedule.exercise: Compare posterior sampling with epsilon-greedy exploration, show how offline data with poor coverage misleads a naive agent, and write a one-page note on an open problem about misspecified models.

tasks.title: Compare posterior sampling and epsilon-greedy on a 10-armed Bernoulli bandit over 1000 rounds, plotting cumulative regret for 50 runs
Learn a policy from a fixed dataset with poor coverage, show overestimated values for unseen actions and fix them with a pessimistic penalty
Plan with a misspecified model after a shift in dynamics, measure the loss against the true-model policy and test one robustness remedy

schedule.title: Constraints, risk and verification
schedule.exercise: Solve a constrained MDP with a safety budget, compare policies optimised for expected return, CVaR and worst case, and model check a policy against a probabilistic safety property.

tasks.title: Compute expected return and CVaR at 10 percent for two policies from simulated return samples, and say which a cautious planner prefers
Solve a constrained grid MDP with a Lagrange multiplier search, and plot return and constraint cost against the multiplier
Solve a robust MDP with an interval uncertainty set, compare it with the nominal policy under perturbed dynamics and report the worst-case value

schedule.title: Planning for robots, agents and field systems
schedule.exercise: Model drone crop spraying with wind uncertainty as a planning problem, choose a solver with justification, and critique how a language-model planner would be verified before field use.

tasks.title: Model ambulance dispatch for a district as an MDP with random calls and run value iteration to find a dispatch policy
Plan a path with a chance constraint on collision probability in a grid with noisy motion, and compare it with a shortest-path plan
Use a language model to propose plans for a delivery domain, verify each against a formal model and measure the rate of unsafe plans caught

schedule.title: Proposal writing and peer review
schedule.exercise: Write a four-page proposal with a problem statement, related work gap, hypotheses, benchmark design and evaluation plan, and defend it to a panel of peers.

tasks.title: Tabulate ten papers by problem setting, assumptions, solver and benchmark, and mark the combinations that nobody has tested
Design a benchmark of five planning problems with controlled difficulty, and justify the metrics, number of seeds and confidence intervals
Run the pilot experiment from a peer's proposal, report whether the baseline behaves as they predicted and suggest two changes
